threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of just 'the train' like the rest of us. That and not knowing where the nearest pub is.
Last night on the 59, a passenger serenaded us all with a full rendition of 'Wonderwall'. A proper Brixton moment, everyone just vibed along.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw kids racing their scooters past a street artist painting a mural, while an old lady played the accordion on the corner. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you see a bus stop that doubles as an art installation, with graffiti that changes weekly. Makes waiting for the M10 much more interesting!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they know the exact time to avoid the 49 bus after 6 PM, or when they instinctively duck into a taco spot during BART delays.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a busker playing 'California Dreamin''—it was raining inside and outside. Perfect SF moment, right in the heart of the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all 'patatas bravas' are the same, but the secret is in the sauce. You can tell a local by what they dip.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they still patiently wait for the light to change at crosswalks, even when there's no cars in sight.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep walking into shops and expecting the staff to say 'hello' instead of staring at you like you're lost. It's a classic Dalston move.
Last night on the N37, a guy was having a full-on debate with the bus driver about the best late-night takeaway in Brixton. Spoiler: they both agreed on the chicken shop.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy serenading his pigeon flock with an accordion at Hermannplatz. Only in Neukölln could this feel so normal.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find late-night bakeries selling fresh bread at 2 AM while the rest of the city sleeps, perfect for a midnight snack run.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know to avoid BART when there's a 'loud bang' at Civic Center—like, that’s a weekly occurrence.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a No. 14 packed to the brim with folks, yet somehow the guy in the back kept trying to sell tacos. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just Gaudí vibes and quirky shops, but miss out on the local bars where the real community breathes.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell who's new by the way they hesitate at the tram stops, trying to decipher the routes while clutching their phones.
